newsitem.title: USA: U.S. corp bond issuance thin ahead of holidays.
newsitem.headline: U.S. corp bond issuance thin ahead of holidays.

text.p: As the countdown to the end of the year continues corporate bond issuance will thin out as only a few preferred securities and high-yield issues are slated to come to market ahead of the holidays, dealers said.
"Generally, it's pretty quiet...trust preferreds seem to be carrying the day here," said one high-grade syndicate source.
"The calendar's going to be very light. The two holidays falling in the middle of the week will keep issuance pretty slim," he added.
Dealers said the majority of supply left consist of a few preferred deals and some junk issues as issuers begin to wrap up their finaning before year end.
"Issues we're hearing about today consists mainly of trust preferreds and junk issues...business is starting to wind down," another high-grade source said.
"Activity's slowing down particularly with treasury supply coming in and as we head into the holidays.
First Tennessee National is expected to issue $100 million in 30-year debt with a call feature in the tenth year via Goldman Sachs & Co, dealers said.
Also, USF&G is expected to issue $100 million in trust preferred securities via Goldman Sachs.
In addition, BTC Capital Securities is expected to set $250 million in capital securities due 2006 via Bear Stearns.

Meanwhile, dealers said with not much left to the calendar year and the Christmas and New Year's holidays approaching the bulk of supply is likely to come this week while desks are still fully staffed.
Also, American Re Corp is expected to tap the market with $500 million in 30-year noncallable 144A debt also via Goldman Sachs & Co. The deal is expected to be rated Aa1/AA.
So far in Thursday's business, Bank of New York issued $300 million in 30-year capital securities to yield 126 basis points over comparable Treasuries via Merrill Lynch & Co.

"It's a perfect environment for issuance but activity so far has been dull," one syndicate source said. "Issuance is certainly beginning to wind down now that the holidays are just around the corner."
Currently, the 30-year U.S. Treasury bond is up 21/32 at 98-1/32 to yield 6.65 percent off from Wednesday's 6.70 percent yield at the close.
Among high-yield debt offerings, Willcox & Gibbs' is expected to issue $85 million in seven-year 144A notes via Dillon Read & Co. Price talk is seen in the 11.50 percent arean.
Meanwhile, among deals expected in the new calendar year are Italy's $1.0 billion 10-year global issue, and State Development Bank of China's $300 million 10-year yankee debt offering, dealers said.
Also, Disney & Co is rumored to come to market in the new year with a $500 million 10-year debt offering of its own, syndicate sources said.
